name: Hubbell

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (Hubbell-corporate primary digital logo color.png, 2000x816 px)

description: Hubbell makes the hardware that moves and protects electricity: grid components such as insulators, connectors, switches, arresters and smart meters sold to electric utilities (Utility Solutions, 63% of sales), and wiring, connectors, enclosures and industrial controls sold to electrical contractors and industrial users, mostly through distributors (Electrical Solutions). It earns money from one-time product sales priced per unit, with a low-single-digit price increase and modest volume change in 2025. Its top ten customers are about 42% of net sales. FY2025 net sales were $5,844.6M (+3.8%) with an operating margin of 20.7%, and it bought DMC Power and Nicor in 2025 for about $885M net of cash.

employees.note: Approximately 18,000 salaried and hourly employees, about 10,900 (61%) in the United States.

businessLines.name: Utility Solutions
businessLines.how: Sells grid components and communication and control products (transmission and distribution hardware, substation parts, meters and advanced metering infrastructure) to electric utilities, mostly via distributors or directly, as one-time product sales priced per unit.

businessLines.name: Electrical Solutions
businessLines.how: Sells wiring devices, connectors, enclosures, cord reels and industrial controls to electrical contractors and industrial customers through electrical and industrial distributors, home centers and retailers; one-time product sales, with data center and non-residential end markets named in the 10-K.

brands.name: Utility Solutions brands
brands.note: Aclara, Chance, Anderson, PenCell, Fargo, Hubbell, Polycast, Quazite, USCO, Ohio Brass, Delmar, Armorcast and others (10-K lists them; no per-brand revenue disclosed).

brands.name: Electrical Solutions brands
brands.note: Bryant, Burndy, Raco, Killark, Wiegmann, Hipotronics, Kellems, TayMac, Gleason Reel, iDevices, Ventev, Bell and others (10-K lists them; no per-brand revenue).

brands.name: DMC Power
brands.note: Acquired 2025-10-01 for about $829 million net of cash; swaged connection systems and tooling for utility substation and transmission; added to Utility Solutions (10-K).

brands.name: Nicor, Inc.
brands.note: Acquired in 2025 (with DMC Power, aggregate purchase price about $885 million net of cash).
